 Judgment
The petitioner has filed claim application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

Mahesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23848880/
1 02.

The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
On 20.04.2023 at about 07.10 a.m, when the petitioner was proceeding in his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-02-KM-9725 from Dasarahalli lake road to go to his work and when he reached NH-4, Tumkur Road, Chokkasandra Signal Service Road, at that time, a KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-06-F-1154 came from 8th Mile to Jalahalli Cross,
belonging to the respondent, driven by its driver in very high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and Motor Cycle.
Due to this impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 after the accident he was shifted to Raghavendra People Tree hospital for first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Rajashekar hospital, JP Nagara, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient for 20 days and underwent several examinations and operated the left leg femur and head injury and inserted the implant and he has spent more than Rs.7,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 23 years, working as centering labour and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he lost the future income, future prospective life and become permanent disabled.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the aforesaid offending KSRTC bus by its driver and in this regard the Peenya Traffic Police have registered a case in Crime No.266/2023 for the offence punishable U/s 279, 337 of IPC and Sec.117 and 119 of MV Act against the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Hence, the respondent being the RC owner and internal insurer of the said offending KSRTC bus is liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, respondent has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed objection.

04. Respondent in its written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied age, occupation, income of the petitioner, manner of the accident,
negligence on the part of the driver of KSRTC bus, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and imaginary and hence pray for dismiss the petition with costs.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed by my learned predecessor: -

sentences.text:
01. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 20.04.2023 at about 07.10 a.m, on Chokkasandra Junction,
NH-4 Road, T.Dasarahalli, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-06-F-1154 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
What Order or Award?
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner was got examined as PW.1 and got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked 25 documents as Ex.P.1 to 25 and closed his side evidence.
07. By way of rebuttal, the driver of the respondent bus got examined as RW.1 and no documents have been marked and closed its side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.

09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In partly affirmative  Issue No.2 In partly affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-
Petitioner filed affidavit as PW.1 by reiterating the petition averments.
During the course of cross-examination, he denied that, due to his negligence, the accident took place.
He denied that there is no negligence by the driver of the KSRTC Bus and accident took place due to his negligence.

On perusal of the documents, Ex.P.1 is the FIR in Crime (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 No.266/2023 registered at Peenya Traffic Police for the offence punishable U/s 279,
338 of IPC and Sec.119 and 177 of MV Act against driver of the KSRTC Bus.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC Bus the accident took place and petitioner sustained injuries.
The public and friends took him to the hospital and admitted as inpatient.
11. The accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus.
Ex.P.3 is the Statement of petitioner which supports the version of Ex.P.2.
Ex.P.4 is Spot Mahazar showing Mahesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23848880/
3 the place of accident on NH-4 Tumkur Road, Chokkasandra- T.Dasarahalli Junction, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is Notice issued U/Sec 133 of IMV Act to the respondent.
Ex.P.6 is Reply given by the respondent stating that one Naveen Kumar was driving the offending KSRTC bus as on the date of accident and he had valid driving licence.
Ex.P.7 is IMV report which shows involvement of the offending bus in the accident.
Ex.P.8 is the Wound certificate which shows the petitioner sustained Head injury:- bleeding per bilateral ear, nose and mouth.
(CT brain - EDH and fascial bone and nasal bone fractured).
Laceration over (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 left thigh, bone (femur fractured) and laceration over left ankle
, said injury Nos.1 and 2 are grievous in nature.
Ex.P.9 is the important document of investigation officer.
After completion of the investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of the KSRTC bus for the above offences.

Ex.P.11 is the discharge summary which shows that the petitioner sustained head injury with diffuse axonal injury and diffuse cerebral edema, SAH/EDH and left side femoral shaft fracture and the injuries are grievous in nature.
Ex
is the Aadhaar card.
The petitioner got examined MRD incharge as PW.3 and he has produced Authorization letter, MLC register extract, Police intimation and inpatient records as per Ex.P.20 to 23.

Doctor PW.2 filed affidavit stating that, petitioner sustained Head injury with diffuse axonal injury and diffuse cerebral oedema - SAH/EDH and left sided femoral shaft fracture (compound M/3rd fracture), said injuries are grievous in nature.
These documents clearly goes to show that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC bus.

12 . Further, to disprove the case of the petitioner, on behalf of the respondent, the driver of the offending KSRTC bus is examined as RW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the written statement averments therein.
During the course of cross-examination by the petitioner counsel he admits that the Police have filed Charge sheet for rash and negligent driving of KSRTC bus against him.
However, respondent counsel argued that as per the below mentioned rulings there is no negligence by the driver and he prays to fix the negligence on the petitioner.
Hence, his contention is untenable.
However, the police documents also very much clear that due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of KSRTC bus accident took place.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

Petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 23 years,
working as (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 centering labour and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.7,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental charges.
Due to accidental injuries, he lost his income, earning capacity and become permanent disabled.
Mahesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 July, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23848880/
4 14.
So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner has not placed any documents or evidence before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of authenticated, believable and satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the injured, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-.
15
. According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his examination in chief.
Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he assessed limb disability at 38% and whole body disability of 19%.
However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 12%.

(SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 16. Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- As per Ex.P.11 Discharge summary, the petitioner was admitted as inpatient on 21.04.2023 and discharged on 10.05.2023,
totally for 19 days.
During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore,
considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
17. Pain and sufferings:
As per Ex.P.8 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 Doctor and as per Ex.P.11 Discharge summary and X-ray and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
18. Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding his income.
This tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.16,000/- per month and he was admitted in the hospital for 19 days as inpatient.

Considering the nature of injuries, (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast three months.
Thus, taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/- (Rs.16,000/- x 2) under this head.

19. Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills as per Ex.P.13, 17 and 25,
which amounts to Rs.4,92,141/-, Rs.36,876/- and Rs.58,859/-.
To disprove the said medical expenses, the respondent has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,87,876/- under this head.
20. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:-

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

Mahesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23848880/
5 21.
Future medical expenses:-

According to doctor, the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implant, which would cost around Rs.40,000/- in a private set up, but he has not produced any estimation (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 regarding future medical expenses.
Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

22. Looking to the nature of the injuries, it is duty of petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show this exact date of birth.
However, he has produced notarized copy of Aadhaar card at Ex.P.15.
Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age for any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon.
On perusal of Ex.P.15, the date of birth of the petitioner mentioned as 04.01.2000 and the alleged accident was occurred on 20.04.2023.
Therefore, considering the said document and police records and medical records, this tribunal has assessed age of the petitioner as 23 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is '18'.

sentences.text: As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s. Pranay Sethi and others 2017(16 SCC 680).

sentences.text: If the petitioner is having self employee, a future prospects has to be considered.
The petitioner was aged 23 years on the date of accident, hence 40% has to be added towards future prospects as Rs.16,000/- + 6,400/- = 22,400/-.
The doctor PW.2 has given disability 38% and 19%, but he admitted in his cross-examination, he has not given the disability compare to the whole body.
So, I have taken 12% of the disability to the whole body.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is as follows.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
 Rs.22,400/- x 12 x 18 x 12/100 =
Rs.5,80,608/-.
24.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-

Sl. Head of compensation Amount in Rs. No.
1. Loss of future income 5,80,608-00 2.
Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00 3.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious 30,000-00 food and conveyance charges (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 Mahesh vs K.S.R.T.C on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23848880/
6 4.
Medical Expenses 5,87,876-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00 unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 32,000-00 period
7. Future medical expenses 30,000-00 Total 13,20,484-00 25.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.13,20,484/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

26. Regarding liability:- The respondent has taken specific contention that the petitioner has seen the bus at a distance of 30 feet and there is humps on the road and he was stopped his bike when he was seen the bus at a distance of 30 feet, this accident would not occurred and the bus was coming in a slow manner and hence, certain decree of contributory negligence will have to be attributed to him.

In this regard, the counsel for the respondent has relied upon the following citations:-
(SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 01. (2007) 5 SCC 428 in a case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Meena Variyal and others,
wherein it is held at para 27 that, "Once they approach the tribunal under section 166 of the Act,
they have necessarily to take upon themselves the burden of establishing the negligence of the driver or owner of the vehicle concerned.

sentences.text: It is crystal clear from the perusal of Ex.P.6 and 7, sketch and panchanama, respectively that the deceased was proceeding from East to West.

When they reached near the end of junction near 4th cross connecting to 2nd stage of RMV Road, the rider of the offending vehicle instead of proceeding straight came to the offside of the road and the deceased also left his track to a little extent on the road resulting in the accident.

Therefore, it establishes beyond reasonable doubt that there is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased as well as on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle having regard to the spot of the accident as seen from the Sketch".
08. MFA No.11124/2005, 11125/2005 and 11126/2005 (MV) in a case of The New India Assurance Co. Ltd., V/s Adivappa Sidram Madar and another, which relates to percentage of disability.

sentences.text:
27. In the case on hand, the petitioner has admitted that he has seen the bus at a distance of 30 feet and there is humps on the road and he was stopped his bike when he was seen the bus at a (SCCH-3)
18 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 distance of 30 feet, it appears that the petitioner also contributed to the accident to the extent of 20% and driver of the offending KSRTC bus is contributed negligent to the extent of 80%.

Hence, the citations relied upon by the respondent is aptly applicable to the case on hand to some extent, because the petitioner has not produced the Spot Sketch showing the negligence is on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus and accordingly, this tribunal has holds that the claimant is also contributed for the accident.
Therefore, the petitioner is contributed 20% to the accident.

Accordingly, out of said compensation amount of Rs.13,20,484/-, Rs.2,64,096/- 20% of compensation amount has to be deducted towards contributory negligent of petitioner, then the petitioner is entitled for remaining compensation amount of Rs.10,56,388/-.

Hence the respondent being the owner and self-insurer of the offending KSRTC Bus is liable to pay compensation amount of Rs.10,56,388/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

(SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.3382/2023 28. Issue No.3:- In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,56,388/- (Rupees Ten lakhs fifty six thousand three hundred and eighty eight only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

8 (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The petitioner is at liberty to draw periodical interest.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
